sahne: Interior of a city bus taking a sharp left turn, photographed from the middle of the aisle looking toward the front. Several standing passengers hold the hanging ceiling hand straps; all of their bodies lean clearly toward the right-hand side of the bus, the outside of the turn, and the unused hanging straps also swing out toward the right. Through the windshield the road visibly curves to the left. A shopping bag on an empty seat has tipped over toward the right. Daylight, realistic photographic style. No text, letters, numbers, route displays, signs or logos anywhere in the image.

Sunny backyard: a teenager stands with feet apart and swings a transparent plastic bucket, half full of blue-tinted water, in a vertical circle with a straight arm. The bucket is captured at the very top of the circle, directly above the person's head and completely upside down, yet the water stays pressed against the bottom of the bucket and not a single drop falls out. A faint circular motion blur traces the rest of the vertical circle beside the person. Green lawn and a wooden fence in the background. No text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere in the image.

A perfectly calm mountain lake at sunrise with no wind at all. Dark pine trees and a rocky mountain peak stand on the far shore, and the still water reflects them exactly upside down, so the whole scene looks mirror-symmetric about the shoreline: the tree tops point downward in the water. A small wooden rowing boat floats near the far shore with its upside-down reflection directly beneath it. A clear sky with a few thin clouds is also mirrored in the water. Photographed at eye level from the near shore, wide angle, sharp detail, no people, no text, letters or numbers.

Inside a classic barbershop: two large flat mirrors hang on OPPOSITE walls, exactly facing and parallel to each other; a barber chair stands between them. Looking into one mirror you see a long receding tunnel of repeated images: the chair seen alternately from the front and from the back, each copy smaller and slightly dimmer and greener than the one before, with the edges of both mirror frames repeating around each copy. Warm light, no text or signs.

Close-up on a light wooden table: a hand holds an ordinary plastic comb a few centimetres above a small scattered pile of tiny torn pieces of white tissue paper. Several paper bits are leaping up from the table toward the comb, some caught in mid-air between table and comb, and a few are already clinging to the comb's teeth. Soft window light from the side, shallow depth of field, the rest of the table softly blurred. No text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere in the image.

Science museum demonstration in a darkened hall: a person stands calmly inside a large cage made of metal wire mesh, arms relaxed at the sides. Bright bluish-white electric sparks from a tall high-voltage generator standing next to the cage strike the outside of the metal mesh and branch over its surface. The person inside is unharmed and relaxed, lit by the flashes. A few visitors are silhouetted in the foreground, watching. No text, letters, numbers, signs or logos anywhere in the image.

A clear semicircular acrylic block lying flat on a sheet of plain white paper on a dark lab bench in a dim room, a thin pencil line drawn on the paper along the normal at the centre of the flat edge. A narrow red light beam from a small ray box on the left enters the CURVED side of the block aimed exactly at the centre of the flat edge, so it goes straight through the curved surface WITHOUT bending, travels along a radius to the centre of the flat edge, and there it is totally reflected back into the block at the same angle on the other side of the normal line; no beam leaves through the flat edge. No text.

Close-up of a thin yellow fiber-optic patch cable on a dark workbench, wound in a very tight small loop around a pencil. A bright red light has been sent into the cable from a small handheld light source at one end, slightly out of focus in the background. At the tight loop the cable jacket glows vivid red where light leaks out, while the straight lengths of cable before and after the loop stay unlit and plain yellow. Dim room so the red glow stands out. No text, no labels, no numbers on the tools or the cable.

A teenager standing upright in a clear outdoor swimming pool, calm water up to the waist, seen from the pool edge from the side and slightly above. The part of the legs below the water surface looks noticeably shorter and stockier than it should, and the outline of the body appears to shift slightly at the water line. The pool floor with plain light-blue square tiles looks shallow, with soft rippling light patterns on it. Bright sunlight. No text, no numbers, no depth markings, no signs.

A tall, clear, straight-sided drinking glass on a white kitchen table, filled with water and topped with a distinct layer of golden cooking oil floating on the water; the boundary between oil and water is a sharp horizontal line. A shiny coin lies flat on the bottom of the glass. Viewed from the side and slightly above, soft daylight from a window. No text, no numbers, no measuring marks on the glass.

A seaside cliff at golden hour, wide side view: a young person on the cliff edge has just thrown a stone forward and slightly upward. The single stone is shown mid-flight, sharp, a little beyond the top of its path, and a faint thin smooth curved trail line marks its path: a short low rise from the hand, then a long curve falling far down toward the sea, clearly asymmetric (the falling part is much longer and steeper than the rising part). No multiple exposures, no text.

A high-school physics classroom demonstration of the classic falling-target experiment. On a lab bench at the left, a small spring-loaded launcher tube points diagonally upward, aimed straight at a soft plush toy monkey that hangs from a small electromagnet on a tall metal stand at the right. A small yellow ball has just left the tube and is in mid-flight; at the same instant the toy has been released and is falling (slight motion blur on both the ball and the toy). The ball is on its way to meet the toy below the toy's original position. A few students watch from the side. Bright daylight classroom, realistic photo, no text, no numbers, no labels.

An indoor badminton hall, side view: a player has just hit a high clear; the shuttlecock's flight appears as a sequence of exposures along an asymmetric path that rises in a long slant and then drops much more steeply near the far end. In EVERY exposure the shuttlecock flies CORK FIRST: the rounded cork tip always points in the direction of motion and the feather skirt trails behind it, both while rising and while falling. No text.

Close-up on a classroom lab bench. A student's hand is quickly pushing a straight bar magnet, painted half red and half blue, into the open end of a large coil made of many visible turns of copper-coloured enamelled wire wound on a clear plastic tube; slight motion blur on the magnet shows that it is moving. Two leads run from the ends of the coil to an old-fashioned analogue galvanometer whose needle is swung clearly to one side of its centre position. The galvanometer dial has only plain tick marks with no numbers or letters, and the magnet has no letters on it. No text, labels, numbers or logos anywhere in the image. Bright daylight classroom, shallow depth of field.

A dimly lit school physics lab. On a wooden bench stands a simple circuit made of a large battery, a big coil of thick copper wire wound around a heavy iron core, and an old-fashioned open knife switch with a wooden handle, all joined by thick leads. A hand has just pulled the copper blade of the knife switch up and away from its contact, and a bright bluish-white spark is jumping across the small gap between the blade and the contact, lighting the scene. No text, labels, numbers or logos anywhere in the image.

A sunny green garden lawn in late afternoon with a single metal garden sprinkler standing in the middle of the grass. The sprinkler head has many small nozzles and sprays thin jets of water outward in all directions at once, forming a round dome of glittering streams around it. The grass right around the sprinkler is dark and soaked, and it looks gradually drier further away toward the edges of the lawn. Water drops sparkle in the low sunlight against a softly blurred hedge in the background. Low camera angle close to the ground, no people, no hoses in the foreground, no text, letters or numbers anywhere.

A dim school physics laboratory. On a long plain wooden rail without any scale markings, two lit incandescent lamps face each other from opposite ends: one is a larger, brighter bulb and the other a small, dimmer bulb. Between them a sheet of white paper stands upright in a simple wooden holder, perpendicular to the rail, and it stands clearly closer to the small dim bulb than to the large bright one. In the center of the paper there is a round translucent grease spot that is barely visible, because both faces of the paper are lit about equally. Seen from the side at the height of the rail so that both lamps and the paper screen are in view. Warm soft light, shallow depth of field, no people, no text, letters, numbers or scale marks.

A clear rectangular glass aquarium filled with water on a lab bench in a darkened classroom, seen from the side at the height of the water surface. A green laser pointer held above the tank on the left sends a thin beam down into the water at a steep slant, about 30 degrees from the vertical. At the water surface the beam bends only SLIGHTLY toward the vertical: in the water it continues at about 22 degrees from the vertical, a gentle, modest bend, not a sharp one. A faint reflected beam goes up from the entry point. Light haze makes the beam visible. No text.

The Sun setting over a calm open sea, its lower edge just touching the flat, sharp horizon line. The solar disk is visibly flattened: noticeably wider than it is tall, with the bottom edge more squashed than the top. Deep orange and red sky near the horizon fading to pale blue higher up, and a glittering path of reflected sunlight on the water leading toward the viewer. No boats, no people, no birds, no text, no numbers.

A sunny outdoor table: a round concave shaving mirror on a stand FACES THE SUN, which is behind the camera and shines straight into the mirror; a hand holds a small piece of brown card in front of the mirror, between the mirror and the sun, slightly off the mirror's axis so it does not block the light, and the reflected sunlight converges to one small, very bright spot on the card. Shadows of the mirror stand fall away from the sun, behind the mirror. No text.

Close-up of a car's exterior side mirror on the driver's side, seen from just behind the driver's shoulder on a sunny day on a two-lane road. The slightly convex mirror glass shows a wide view of the road behind: a following car appears small and far away, together with the neighboring lane, part of the road edge and roadside trees, all bending slightly toward the edges of the mirror. Nothing is printed or etched on the mirror glass. No text, letters, numbers, license plates or logos.

A road cyclist in a deep aerodynamic tuck, riding a racing bicycle fixed on a stationary stand inside a wind tunnel, seen exactly from the side. Several thin, parallel, bright white smoke streams come in from the left at the height of the rider, flow smoothly over the helmet, shoulders and curved back, and break into swirls and small eddies just behind the rider. Dark matte tunnel walls and floor, cool even studio lighting so the smoke lines stand out clearly against the dark background. No text, letters, numbers, logos, screens or measuring displays anywhere in the image.

A tidy high-school physics bench seen from slightly above. A straight, thick, bare copper wire is stretched horizontally between two small wooden stands, a hand's width above the tabletop. Red and black leads connect its two ends through a push-button switch to a battery pack. A small round magnetic compass sits on the table directly beneath the wire; the wire runs along the direction the needle would normally point. A student's finger is pressing the switch, and the compass needle (one half red, one half white) has swung round to point almost perpendicular to the wire instead of along it. The compass face is plain, with no letters, numbers or markings. No text, labels, numbers or logos anywhere in the image. Bright daylight classroom, shallow depth of field.

A classic classroom demonstration on a lab bench: two long, narrow strips of shiny aluminium foil hang vertically side by side, a few centimetres apart, clamped between two horizontal wooden bars on a stand. The circuit is clearly readable: a red wire from the battery's positive terminal goes to the TOP of the left strip, both strips are connected in PARALLEL so they carry current in the SAME direction: a red wire from the battery splits and goes to the top of BOTH strips, and a black wire joins the bottom of BOTH strips back to the battery. Because the currents are parallel, the two strips bow GENTLY toward each other in the middle, still clearly separated by a small gap, not touching. Bright lab, no text.

A darkened physics laboratory. A large clear glass sphere (a fine-beam tube filled with thin gas) sits on a stand between two large, vertical, circular copper coils mounted face to face on each side of it (Helmholtz coils). Inside the sphere a SINGLE thin glowing blue-green electron beam spirals as a regular helix along the axis joining the two coils: all turns of the helix have the SAME diameter and the same spacing. There is NO straight beam through the middle, only the one helical beam. No text.

A dimly lit school physics lab. On a table lies a long metal optical rail with only plain evenly spaced tick marks, no numbers. On the left end of the rail a lit white candle stands in a holder; in the middle a round clear glass lens that is thicker in the centre than at the edges stands upright in a holder; on the right a flat white cardboard screen stands upright. The lens is noticeably closer to the candle than to the screen. On the screen there is a sharp, enlarged, upside-down image of the candle flame: the glowing flame points downward and the top of the candle appears above it. Warm light, realistic photo. No text, numbers, labels or logos anywhere.

A bright school biology and physics lab. A high-school student leans over a white desk and looks with one eye into the eyepiece at the top of a standard light microscope. The microscope is shown clearly from the side: the short eyepiece tube at the top near the student's eye, the long body tube, the rotating nosepiece with three objective lenses of different lengths pointing down just above a thin glass slide on the stage, and a small lamp under the stage shining upward. No text, numbers, labels or logos anywhere, including on the microscope.

A clear rectangular glass aquarium half filled with still, clean water stands on a table. A card with a plain black-and-white checkerboard pattern is placed flat against the outside of the aquarium's back wall. A hand holds a round magnifying lens without a handle frame vertically inside the aquarium, parallel to the front wall, so that the water surface crosses the lens horizontally through its middle: the upper half of the lens is in air, the lower half is under water. Seen from the front, the checkerboard squares behind the upper, in-air half of the lens look strongly enlarged, while the squares behind the lower, underwater half look only slightly larger than the squares around the lens. Soft daylight, realistic photo. No text, numbers, labels or logos anywhere.

Inside the bright, cluttered module of a space station in orbit: an astronaut floats weightlessly, feet hooked under a foot rail, and pushes with both hands against a large white storage cabinet-sized cargo container that is also floating in mid-air. The astronaut's arms are bent and the shoulders braced, clearly putting in real effort, and the big container has only just started to drift slowly away. Next to the astronaut's head a small drink pouch floats freely. Cables, handrails and equipment panels line the walls. Realistic photo style, no text, no numbers, no labels, no flags, no mission patches.

High-speed sports photograph, side view close-up at grass level: a football player's boot striking a football at the instant of contact. The ball is visibly squashed and flattened where the boot presses into it, and a few blades of grass and tiny water droplets fly off. Background is a softly blurred stadium. Frozen motion, crisp detail on the deformed ball, no text, no numbers, no logos, no sponsor marks, no readable ball branding.

A high-school physics lab bench photographed from the side at table height: a small low-friction wheeled lab cart sits on a smooth horizontal track on the table. A thin string is tied to the front of the cart, runs horizontally to a small pulley clamped at the edge of the table, passes over it and hangs straight down, holding a small slotted metal mass hanger with a couple of weights. The hanging mass has just started to fall and the cart has just started to roll toward the pulley (slight motion blur on both). The string is taut. Clean lab setting, soft daylight, realistic photo, no text, no numbers, no scale markings, no labels.

A darkened high-school physics lab, seen from slightly above a table. A small triangular glass prism stands with one of its triangular faces flat on a round rotating turntable; the turntable rim has only plain evenly spaced tick marks, no numbers or letters. The prism's apex points toward the back of the table and its base faces the camera. A thin red laser beam, made visible by a light haze, comes from a laser pointer on the left, travels just above the tabletop, enters the prism's left side face, and leaves through the right side face bent toward the camera side, toward the prism's base, so the outgoing beam is clearly not in line with the incoming one. The outgoing beam ends as a bright red dot on a white vertical screen on the right. A student's hand rests on the edge of the turntable, slowly turning it. No text, numbers, labels or logos anywhere.

A dark optics bench seen from the side at table height. A triangular glass prism stands upright with its apex pointing UP and its base on the table. Three thin parallel horizontal laser beams (red on top, green in the middle, violet at the bottom) enter the left face of the prism. EVERY beam is bent DOWNWARD, toward the prism's base, both on entering and on leaving the prism, so all three leave the right face angled downward, below their original horizontal line: the red beam is bent the LEAST (shallowest downward angle), the green a bit more, the violet the MOST (steepest downward angle). No beam goes upward. The three beams hit a white screen on the right as three dots, all lower than where they started. Faint haze makes the beams visible. No text.

Two high-school students at a classroom desk doing the ruler-drop reaction test: one student holds a long wooden ruler vertically by its top end at eye level; the other student's thumb and index finger are open around the bottom end of the ruler, not touching it, ready to catch. The ruler has just been released and is falling straight down (slight motion blur on the ruler), the catcher's fingers just beginning to close. The ruler shows only plain tick marks, no numbers or letters. Bright daylight classroom, shallow depth of field.

A snowy park on a bright winter day, side view of two identical wooden sleds, each carrying the same small cardboard box as a load, moving left to right side by side on flat, packed snow. On the upper sled, one child walks in front and pulls it with a rope held at shoulder height, so the rope rises clearly upward at an angle from the front of the sled to the child's hand. On the lower sled, a second child walks behind and pushes it with straight arms angled downward onto the back of the sled, leaning forward. Both children are wearing winter coats and hats. Realistic photo, soft winter light, no text, no numbers, no signs.

A quiet dry asphalt road on an overcast day, viewed from slightly above and behind a small hatchback car that has just come to a stop after an emergency brake. Behind each of its front wheels, two long, dark black skid marks stretch back along the lane in straight parallel lines, gradually fading toward the far end. The car's brake lights are on. No other traffic, no people. Realistic photo, no text, no numbers, no licence plate characters, no road signs with writing, no logos.

Two opened power adapters lie side by side on a light wooden workbench, both with their plastic cases removed and the case halves set beside them. On the left, an old, heavy wall adapter whose inside is almost entirely filled by one chunky transformer: a thick stack of grey laminated iron sheets with bulky copper windings. On the right, a modern compact phone charger whose small green circuit board carries only a tiny transformer with a dark ferrite core, far smaller than the old one, among a few small electronic parts. Soft daylight from the side. No text, labels, brand names, numbers or logos anywhere in the image.
